analysis.brief_en: This article reports a case of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) in a 76-year-old male patient from Hefei, Anhui, China, who presented with fever, fatigue, and anorexia on May 27, 2025. The patient had a history of agricultural work and chronic hepatitis B with low-level viral replication. He was diagnosed with SFTS, liver injury, myocardial injury, and invasive pulmonary aspergillosis and mucormycosis coinfection. Initial treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin, hepatoprotective therapy, and antiviral therapy stabilized his condition. Subsequently, he was treated with oral isavuconazole combined with nebulized amphotericin B, which led to significant clinical and radiological improvement. However, approximately one month after isavuconazole therapy, the patient developed jaundice and coagulation dysfunction, which were considered probable as drug-induced liver injury. The case underscores the susceptibility of SFTS patients to invasive fungal infections due to immune dysregulation and highlights the importance of liver function monitoring in such patients. The case fatality rate for SFTS ranges from 10% to 30%, and the patient's condition improved with the treatment, with pulmonary lesions resolving after two months.
